accounts.name: new_authority
docs: No key maps to [`ZERO_ADDRESS`], so this constraint alone refuses an
accept while no rotation is pending.

accounts.name: authority
docs: Either of the maker's keys. The handler matches them, since anchor's
`address =` locks to one key. The hot key covers withdrawal so the
quoting loop does not need the cold key. The config key covers it
when the maker no longer trusts the hot key.

accounts.name: authority
docs: The maker's config key. It pauses the instance, reconfigures it, and
rotates the hot key. It is independent of the quoted user, so a desk can
hold it cold, or share one operator key across the wallets it quotes
for.

accounts.name: user_authority
docs: The quoted wallet. Its signature is the consent to quote its sub-account,
which velocity's registry enforces on Custom-entry creation. The address
seeds the PDA, so only one instance exists per market, wallet and
sub-account, and the binding is immutable once set.

accounts.name: execute_authority
docs: The only signer `execute_v0` accepts. It is velocity's quoter CPI signer
PDA, and it is immutable after creation. It arrives as an account and
not as an argument, because a duplicated account costs one index byte in
the transaction.

accounts.name: hot_authority
docs: The hot key for mid and level writes. `authority` can rotate it.

accounts.name: new_authority
docs: The proposed next config key. It gains no power until it signs
`accept_authority_v0`, so a mistyped target cannot lock the maker out
of its own instance.

accounts.name: quoter
docs: Mutable only for the response tail. The ladder is not written.

accounts.name: authority
docs: The maker's config key. It is the only key that can reconfigure the
instance, and no instruction reassigns it, so the maker keeps the pause
control. It is not the quoted wallet. The quoted user seeds the PDA and
is fixed at creation, so no config update can send fills to a different
`User`.

accounts.name: new_hot_authority
docs: When present, this account becomes the new hot key.

errors.name: InvalidAuthority
errors.msg: Signer does not match the quoter authority for this operation

errors.name: TooManyLevels
errors.msg: More levels than the ladder holds

errors.name: LevelsNotAscending
errors.msg: Level offsets must be strictly ascending

errors.name: StaleMidSequence
errors.msg: Nonzero mid sequence must strictly increase

errors.name: InvalidInstructionsSysvar
errors.msg: Deprecated: the protected-flow claim rides the wire, not a sysvar

errors.name: InvalidVelocityState
errors.msg: Deprecated: this program reads no velocity account

errors.name: OversizedUserSet
errors.msg: User set holds more entries than USER_SET_CAPACITY

fields.name: clear_mid
docs: Also zero the mid, which stops every side from quoting whatever the
ladders hold. See `MidpointQuoterV0::is_quoting`. The stop is not
durable: the hot key can stamp a new mid at once. The durable stop
is `update_quoter_v0 { is_paused: true }`, set and cleared only by the config key.

types.name: CancelAllOutcomeV0
docs: What a `cancel_all_v0` withdrew. It carries rung counts and nothing more.
Unlike the CLOB sweep, this one reserves nothing on velocity's side, so no
caller has aggregates to unwind. A total of the withdrawn intent would mean
reading every rung back, which costs more per rung than the withdrawal.

fields.name: bid_rungs
docs: Rungs withdrawn per side.

fields.name: mid_cleared
docs: Whether the mid was zeroed too.

types.name: CancelSidesV0
docs: Which sides a `cancel_all_v0` withdraws. The wire cannot express "neither",
which would leave a maker believing its quotes are gone. A book reads a side
as a book side and a caller as a position direction. Only the tags must agree.

types.name: DirectionV0
docs: Taker direction, from the taker's perspective. Encoded as its discriminant,
`Long = 0`. A direction inverted across the boundary fills the wrong side.

types.name: ExecuteArgsV0
docs: Arguments to `execute_v0`: commit a fill. [`QuoteArgsV0`] without the price
bound, because `size` is depth the caller chose off the ladder. A quoter may
fill less than `size`, and what it filled is the sum of its balance changes.
Every field must carry the value its quote carried.

fields.name: users
docs: Same contract as [`QuoteArgsV0::users`], and it leads for the same
reason.

fields.name: reference_price
docs: The mark the quote was taken against. A different price makes a quoter
that spends budgets pass over a different set of orders than it quoted.

types.name: MidpointConfigRecordV0
docs: One per config-mutating instruction: `update_quoter_v0`,
`propose_authority_v0` and `accept_authority_v0`. Every one of them emits
the whole config rather than a diff, so a reader never has to replay
earlier records to know the instance's current shape.

fields.name: pending_authority
docs: [`crate::state::ZERO_ADDRESS`] when no rotation is pending.

fields.name: version
docs: [`MIDPOINT_EVENT_VERSION`].

fields.name: user_authority
docs: The quoted wallet, `MidpointQuoterV0::user_authority`. The maker's
config authority is not in the record. It is not part of the fill.

fields.name: configured_market_index
docs: The market index this instance was created for. It rides the PDA seeds,
so it is fixed, not proof of where the fill settled. Velocity's registry
decides the settled market and matches the balance-change user against it
before settling, so no value here turns on this field.

fields.name: direction
docs: 0 is Long, which means the taker bought the ask side. 1 is Short.

fields.name: version
docs: [`MIDPOINT_EVENT_VERSION`].

fields.name: authority
docs: The maker's config key. It pauses, reconfigures and rotates the hot
key, and it signs creation. Nothing reassigns it, so the maker keeps
the kill switch. It is independent of `user_authority`, so a desk can
hold it cold.

fields.name: hot_authority
docs: The key allowed to write the mid and the levels. `authority` rotates
it. The key that signs thousands of mid updates a day carries no other
power.

fields.name: execute_authority
docs: The only signer allowed to execute. It is velocity's quoter CPI signer
PDA. Velocity clamps size to the quoted user's margin before it calls
here. The field never changes after init.

fields.name: user_authority
docs: Wallet half of the quoted velocity `User`. Fills settle against
`(user_authority, user_sub_account_id)`. It signs creation and is part
of the PDA seeds, so quoting a different wallet needs a new instance.

fields.name: mid_price
docs: Mid price, in the market's price precision. Velocity perps use a
PRICE_PRECISION of 1e6. Zero means the instance does not quote.

fields.name: mid_slot
docs: Slot of the last mid write. The staleness gate reads it.

fields.name: mid_sequence
docs: Monotonic guard for racing mid writers. See
[`MidpointQuoterV0::set_mid`].

fields.name: max_mid_staleness_slots
docs: Quotes go empty once `mid_slot` falls this many slots behind.

fields.name: price_tick_size
docs: Quote prices round to a multiple of this, away from mid. It uses the
same price precision as `mid_price`.

fields.name: size_step
docs: Quoted sizes floor to a multiple of this (base precision).

fields.name: min_quote_size
docs: The quoter does not quote a level remainder below this. The value is
in base precision. It floors the base size of a rung despite the name.

fields.name: base_precision
docs: Base units per whole unit. It is always [`BASE_PRECISION`]. See there
for why an instance cannot choose another value.

fields.name: user_sub_account_id
docs: Sub-account half of the quoted user's identity. `user_authority` is
the wallet half.

fields.name: market_index
docs: Velocity perp market index this quoter serves.

fields.name: is_paused
docs: The maker's kill switch on the config path. The registry's `is_active`
is the velocity-side one.

fields.name: require_attested_flow
docs: Quote only protected flow. The taker's flow must serve a window before
the call, either the swift hold or the book's activation delay.
Velocity asserts the fact on the wire as `taker_served_window`. This
program trusts its caller for it, as it does for `users` and `caps`.

fields.name: max_mid_deviation_ppm
docs: The largest `|mid − reference_price| / reference_price` the quoter
fills at, in parts per million. `validate` rejects zero, so the bound
can never be disabled. The config key owns the field, so a compromised
hot key cannot move the mid past this band around velocity's oracle.

fields.name: pending_authority
docs: Proposed next `authority`, or [`ZERO_ADDRESS`] when no rotation is
pending. `authority` stays the signer until `accept_authority_v0`
completes the swap, so a mistyped target cannot lock the maker out.

fields.name: padding
docs: Room for one more pubkey and a scalar or two. A future field lands
here without moving the ladders or the response tail.

fields.name: response
docs: The region `quote_v0` and `execute_v0` stream their wincode response
into. Return data carries a [`ResponsePointerV0`] to it.

types.name: QuoteArgsV0
docs: Arguments to `quote_v0`: what a taker wants, and who the caller can settle
against. `users` is a slice into the caller's instruction data, so a quoter
walks it without a copy in a 4 KB frame. It leads the struct to keep its
offset even, and a field added ahead of it must preserve that.

fields.name: users
docs: The loaded-user set, at most [`USER_SET_CAPACITY`] entries. A reader
checks that with [`user_set_within_capacity`], because the count comes
off the wire.

fields.name: size
docs: Base the taker wants filled.

fields.name: reference_price
docs: The price the caller marks a filled position at, in PRICE_PRECISION.
Only [`UserCapV0`] budgets are spent against it. It does not bound what a
quoter may fill at.

fields.name: taker
docs: The taker's own user, whose resting liquidity is skipped
unconditionally (self-trade prevention).

fields.name: limit_price
docs: The worst price the caller will fill at, in PRICE_PRECISION. Zero means
no bound. Not a trust boundary: a quoter that ignores it returns levels
the caller drops, and never widens what it may fill.

fields.name: taker_served_window
docs: Whether the taker's flow served a protection window before this call:
the swift hold, or the book's activation delay. The caller asserts it. A
quoter that serves only protected flow refuses when this is false.

fields.name: include_taker_origin_reservations
docs: Fill the depth that a taker-origin order reserves. Only the crank that
settles the cross sets it. A quoter that reserves no depth ignores it.

types.name: QuoterConfigV0
docs: Config that init sets and that changes rarely. The addresses ride the
accounts list, because a duplicated account costs one index byte in the
transaction.

fields.name: max_mid_deviation_ppm
docs: The largest `|mid - reference_price| / reference_price` the instance
fills at, in parts per million. It must be nonzero at creation, so a
compromised hot key cannot fill the maker at an off-market mid. The
config key can set it to zero later through `update_quoter_v0`.

types.name: ResponsePointerV0
docs: Where in its response account a quoter wrote the response: the return data of
`quote_v0` and `execute_v0`. Declared once, so no two quoters can disagree
about which `u32` comes first.

fields.name: mid
docs: When present, the write also stamps a new mid, so a shape move and a
mid move stay atomic. The sequence rule from `set_mid_v0` applies.

fields.name: bids
docs: Sides to replace. Writing a side resets its `filled` counters.

fields.name: mid
docs: PRICE_PRECISION. 0 stops quoting.

fields.name: sequence
docs: An optional monotonic guard for racing writers. A nonzero sequence must
strictly increase. A sequence of 0 skips the check only while no writer
has stamped a sequence yet. A mid of 0 is a withdrawal, so it skips the
guard whatever the sequence holds.

types.name: SplineLevelInputV0
docs: A maker's spline-level input on the wire. The program owns `filled`, so
the setter takes only the shape.

types.name: SplineLevelV0
docs: One rung of the spline. It holds standing intent `size` at `mid ± offset`.
`filled` counts what executes consumed since the maker wrote the side.

fields.name: offset_ppm
docs: Distance from mid toward this side, in parts per million of mid.
Offsets ascend strictly within a side. Zero quotes at mid itself.

fields.name: size
docs: Intent size, in the market's base precision.

fields.name: filled
docs: Base consumed since the maker last wrote the side.

fields.name: max_mid_staleness_slots
docs: Bounded by `MidpointQuoterV0::validate` to a nonzero value at or below
`MAX_MID_STALENESS_SLOTS_CEILING`.

fields.name: require_attested_flow
docs: Quote only flow that served a protection window. The claim arrives on
the wire as `taker_served_window`, and this program trusts its caller
for it the way it trusts `users` and `caps`. Enabling it configures no
flow key here and reads no velocity account.

fields.name: max_mid_deviation_ppm
docs: The maximum mid deviation from velocity's oracle, in parts per million.
`MidpointQuoterV0::validate` rejects 0 on every path, so a compromised
hot key can never disable the bound.

fields.name: mid_sequence
docs: New value for the racing-writer sequence counter. Any value is legal,
including a lower one. The counter only rises through `set_mid_v0`; a
writer that sends `u64::MAX` by mistake blocks all later mid writes,
and only the config key can reset it. Stop racing writers before a reset.

types.name: UserCapV0
docs: What one named user may still lose on the swept side, in quote. The quoter
has each fill price and the caller does not, so the cap is not in base. The
quoter charges `base * |price - reference_price| / BASE_PRECISION` where the
fill moves against the owner. Zero belongs in the exclusion bitmap.

fields.name: quote_cap
docs: `u64::MAX` is unbounded. It bounds depth that was margin-reserved at
placement. Base cannot express that bound, because a fill at a price in
the owner's favour costs nothing per base.

fields.name: base_cap
docs: The most base this user may give up on the swept side. `u64::MAX` is
unbounded. A book enforces it at match time and will not fill a reduce-only
order whose owner has no cap here, so for a book this field is a trust
boundary. Every other quoter reads it as advisory.

fields.name: index
docs: Index into the accompanying user set.

types.name: UserCapsV0
docs: Per-user room, parallel to the caller's user set. A user absent from all of
this is unconstrained. The quoter skips an excluded user's orders, and an
exclusion never fails the call. Not a trust boundary: the caller's own
post-fill checks still refuse the fill.

fields.name: excluded
docs: One bit per index in the set: set means no room on the swept side, so
pass that user's orders over.

fields.name: len
docs: Live entries at the head of `caps`. The tail is undefined.

types.name: UserRefV0
docs: A velocity user in derivable form: the wallet and sub-account index that both
the `User` and `UserStats` PDAs derive from. An off-chain reader can reach every
user-derived account from a quoter's state alone. A stored `User` key cannot,
because its authority lives in account data the reader cannot load.
